1.1.1.183.rationale: Geraniol dehydrogenase is a simple NADP-dependent oxidoreductase in monoterpene catabolism with no literature suggesting a second catalytic domain.

1.1.1.195.rationale: Cinnamyl-alcohol/coniferyl-alcohol dehydrogenase (CAD) is a well-studied single-activity lignin-pathway oxidoreductase with no reported fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.2.evidence: PMID 33441766 describes an atypical bifunctional Fe-ADH but is not representative of EC 1.1.1.2 generally; defaulted to monofunctional

1.1.1.21.rationale: Aldose reductase/alditol:NAD+ oxidoreductase (aldo-keto reductase family); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.213.evidence: PMID 7515872 (broad-substrate 'multifunctional roles', not a fused second activity); defaulted to monofunctional

1.1.1.215.rationale: 5-dehydro-D-gluconate:NADP+ 2-oxidoreductase returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.219.rationale: Dihydroflavonol 4-reductase (DFR), a flavonoid/anthocyanin biosynthesis enzyme, is a well-known standalone NADPH-dependent reductase; the 32 EuropePMC hits were pathway-level transcriptomics/metabolomics papers (tea, alfalfa, pomegranate, Portulaca) mentioning DFR among many genes, with no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.221.rationale: This obscure plant oxidoreductase (ionol-related) returned zero literature hits suggesting a second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.1.222.rationale: Phenyllactate dehydrogenase is a single-activity aromatic 2-hydroxyacid dehydrogenase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found.

1.1.1.227.rationale: (-)-Borneol:NAD+ oxidoreductase (borneol dehydrogenase) returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.234.rationale: (2S)-Flavan-4-ol:NADP+ 4-oxidoreductase hits were unrelated plant stress/transcriptomics studies; no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity was found.

1.1.1.237.rationale: Aromatic-lactate dehydrogenase (phenyllactate dehydrogenase family member) is a single-activity oxidoreductase; no fused second catalytic activity reported in the literature.

1.1.1.270.rationale: This NAD-dependent sterol dehydrogenase (ergosterol-pathway type) returned only incidental co-occurrence hits (ergosterol/astaxanthin engineering papers) with no description of a fused second catalytic domain.

1.1.1.271.rationale: GDP-L-fucose synthase (GDP-L-fucose:NADP+ 4-oxidoreductase, 3,5-epimerizing) performs an epimerization plus reduction, but both steps are encompassed by the single EC 1.1.1.271 designation at one active site rather than two classically separate EC-numbered activities fused together; EuropePMC hits (fucose metabolism/salvage pathway papers) show no evidence of a distinct second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.1.274.rationale: 2-dehydro-D-gluconate:NADP+ 2-oxidoreductase hits were unrelated (EC annotation ambiguity commentary, Salmonella comparative genomics); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.285.rationale: This dehydrogenase acts in the plant deoxymugineic acid (phytosiderophore) biosynthesis pathway as a single-activity NAD-dependent oxidoreductase; no fusion evidence found.

1.1.1.287.rationale: D-arabinitol:NADP+ oxidoreductase returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.325.rationale: L-threo-7,8-dihydrobiopterin:NADP+ oxidoreductase is a single-activity dehydrogenase involved in tetrahydrobiopterin regeneration/salvage; no fusion evidence found.

1.1.1.86.evidence: PMID 15654896 ('Probing the mechanism of the bifunctional enzyme ketol-acid reductoisomerase...') — single EC, obligate two-step mechanism, not a fusion of two separately-numbered enzymes

1.1.1.87.rationale: Homoisocitrate dehydrogenase (decarboxylating) had only one unrelated hit (Euglena metabolic pathway review); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.90.rationale: Cyclohexanol:NAD+ oxidoreductase search returned only unrelated hits (fermentation microbiome, olive-oil aldehyde synthase papers); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.3.28.rationale: Inosine:oxygen 5'-oxidoreductase is a simple single-activity oxidase; no literature found describing a second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.3.40.rationale: Mannitol:oxygen oxidoreductase (cyclizing) is a single-activity flavin oxidase; no fusion evidence found.

1.1.3.9.rationale: Galactose oxidase is a single-activity copper radical oxidase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found (zero relevant hits).

1.1.5.4.rationale: FAD-dependent malate dehydrogenase (membrane-associated quinone-linked dehydrogenase) search returned only unrelated genome/metabolism papers; no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.5.8.rationale: Quinate dehydrogenase (quinone, PQQ/membrane-bound type) search returns a single unrelated Candida albicans multi-omics paper; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.99.11.rationale: Mannitol dehydrogenase (cytochrome-linked) is a standalone oxidoreductase. No literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.99.18.evidence: PMID:23329127 (describes the flavocytochrome two-domain architecture of CDH as a single biocatalyst, not two distinct catalytic activities)

1.1.99.28.rationale: D-glucose:D-fructose oxidoreductase (periplasmic glucose-fructose oxidoreductase, e.g. in Zymomonas) is a single-activity enzyme; no fusion evidence found.

1.1.99.5.rationale: sn-Glycerol-3-phosphate:(acceptor) oxidoreductase (membrane-bound glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, GlpD/GlpABC) search returned only unrelated genomics/lipid-metabolism papers; no fused second catalytic activity described.

1.10.3.1.rationale: Catechol oxidase (diphenol oxidase) is a single-activity type-3 copper oxidase; no literature describing a fused second catalytic activity was found.

3.6.3.42.rationale: ATP phosphohydrolase (transport-linked ATPase) activity; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found for this EC.

3.6.3.44.rationale: Generic ABC-type transport ATPase (ATP phosphohydrolase); searches returned no reports of a fused second catalytic activity beyond ATP hydrolysis coupled to transport.

3.6.3.47.rationale: ATP phosphohydrolase (P-type ATPase) search returned zero hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

3.7.1.3.rationale: Kynureninase (L-kynurenine hydrolase) is a standalone PLP-dependent enzyme; retrieved hits (pathway-reconstruction papers) gave no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

3.7.1.8.rationale: 2,6-dioxo-6-phenylhexa-3-enoate benzoylhydrolase (BphD-type meta-cleavage product hydrolase in biphenyl/PCB degradation) showed no literature evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

3.7.1.9.rationale: 2-hydroxymuconate-semialdehyde formylhydrolase is a single hydrolase activity in the catechol meta-cleavage pathway; the single EuropePMC hit was an unrelated soil pollution paper, no bifunctional evidence.

4.1.1.1.rationale: Pyruvate decarboxylase is a single-activity thiamine-diphosphate-dependent decarboxylase central to fermentation; no literature describes a fused second catalytic activity for this EC.

4.1.1.15.rationale: Glutamate decarboxylase (GAD) is a well-characterized PLP-dependent enzyme with a single decarboxylase activity; no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

4.1.1.28.rationale: Aromatic-L-amino-acid (tryptophan) decarboxylase acts on multiple substrates (L-DOPA, 5-HTP, tryptophan) via a single decarboxylation mechanism; no literature describes a second, distinct fused catalytic activity.

4.1.1.65.rationale: Phosphatidylserine decarboxylase (PISD); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

4.1.1.77.rationale: 4-Oxalocrotonate decarboxylase functions within a multi-enzyme catabolic pathway (e.g. with 4-oxalocrotonate tautomerase) but literature describes these as separate interacting enzymes, not a single fused bifunctional polypeptide.

4.1.1.93.rationale: Pyrrole-2-carboxylate decarboxylase is a narrowly characterized enzyme with no literature suggesting a second fused catalytic activity.

4.1.2.13.rationale: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase has a single aldolase catalytic activity; reported secondary roles (e.g. cytoskeletal/V-ATPase binding) are non-catalytic moonlighting functions, not a second fused catalytic activity.

4.1.2.27.rationale: Sphingosine-1-phosphate lyase is a single-activity PLP-dependent lyase; no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

4.1.2.30.rationale: This EC corresponds to the 17,20-lyase activity of cytochrome P450c17 (CYP17A1), which is extensively documented to carry a second, distinct fused catalytic activity, 17alpha-hydroxylase (EC 1.14.14.19), in the same polypeptide; deficiency of both activities together is a well-known clinical entity ('combined 17alpha-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency').

4.1.2.38.rationale: Benzaldehyde lyase is a single-activity ThDP-dependent lyase widely used in biocatalysis; no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

4.1.3.17.evidence: PMID 20843800 (notes secondary oxaloacetate decarboxylation/proton-exchange activity at the same active site, not termed bifunctional)
4.1.3.17.rationale: 4-Hydroxy-4-methyl-2-oxoglutarate/4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate aldolase (RraA-family) also shows oxaloacetate decarboxylation and pyruvate alpha-proton exchange side-activities, but these occur at the same single active site via the same class II metal-dependent mechanism (mechanistic promiscuity), and the literature does not describe them as a classically fused two-domain bifunctional enzyme; RraA's separate RNase E regulatory role is non-catalytic moonlighting.

4.1.3.3.rationale: N-acetylneuraminate lyase (sialic acid aldolase) literature covers its biosynthetic/biotechnological role but no fused second catalytic activity on a single polypeptide.

4.2.1.104.rationale: Cyanate hydratase (cyanase) is a single-activity lyase with no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

4.2.1.107.rationale: This hydro-lyase activity on trihydroxycholestanoyl-CoA is one of the two catalytic activities of the peroxisomal D-bifunctional protein (MFE-2), which fuses 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase 2 and (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activities in a single polypeptide for bile-acid/fatty-acid beta-oxidation.

4.2.1.114.rationale: 2-Hydroxybutane-1,2,4-tricarboxylate hydro-lyase (a homocitrate/homoaconitate-type dehydratase in lysine/coenzyme biosynthesis pathways) is a single-activity hydro-lyase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found.

4.2.1.119.rationale: This EC has very sparse literature coverage (example reaction name is only a KEGG reaction ID, R05595, with no clear common name surfaced by search); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity was found, so it defaults to monofunctional.

4.2.1.131.rationale: Lycopene hydro-lyase (carotenoid hydratase, e.g. CrtC) search returns only a general hydratase-biocatalysis review with no mention of a fused second catalytic activity for this specific enzyme.

4.2.1.17.evidence: UniProt Q08426 (EHHADH); PMID 41500837, 39088276, 40790338 (mitochondrial trifunctional protein / HADHA)
4.2.1.17.rationale: Enoyl-CoA hydratase activity is one of three catalytic domains (hydratase + Delta3,Delta2-enoyl-CoA isomerase EC 5.3.3.8 + 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase EC 1.1.1.35) fused on the single-polypeptide peroxisomal enzyme EHHADH; it is also the HADHA (alpha-subunit) activity of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein complex, paired with the HADHB thiolase subunit.

4.2.1.22.rationale: Cystathionine beta-synthase has a single PLP-dependent catalytic activity; its heme-binding and AdoMet-sensing CBS domains are regulatory, not a second catalytic activity.

4.2.1.3.evidence: PMID:39337438 (review of mitochondrial/cytosolic aconitase functions, describes IRP1 moonlighting as RNA-binding, not catalytic)
4.2.1.3.rationale: Aconitase catalyzes a single isomerization (citrate <-> isocitrate via cis-aconitate); cytosolic aconitase doubles as iron regulatory protein-1 (IRP1), an RNA-binding moonlighting role, not a second catalytic activity.

4.2.1.30.rationale: Glycerol dehydratase (B12-dependent) is a heterotrimeric enzyme carrying a single dehydration activity; no literature surfaced describing a second fused catalytic activity.

4.2.1.33.rationale: 3-Isopropylmalate dehydratase (isopropylmalate isomerase, LeuC/LeuD) is an aconitase-family enzyme whose single catalytic activity is split across two subunits, not two distinct fused activities; search hits concerned unrelated aconitase-superfamily enzymes.

4.2.1.66.rationale: Search for this EC returned almost no specific literature (one generic review on multidomain chimeric enzymes in general); no evidence found of a fused second catalytic activity for this lyase.

4.2.1.74.evidence: PMID 8323290 (trifunctional beta-oxidation complex explicitly linked to EC 4.2.1.74); PMID 41500837 (Mitochondrial Trifunctional Protein deficiency); PMID 39012716 (analogous M. tuberculosis trifunctional enzyme)
4.2.1.74.rationale: Long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase (EC 4.2.1.74) is the hydratase activity of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (MTP/TFP, HADHA/HADHB), a hetero-tetrameric complex where the alpha-subunit fuses long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity and is stably complexed with the beta-subunit's 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activity; this is explicitly described in the literature as a 'trifunctional beta-oxidation complex' and causes 'Mitochondrial Trifunctional Protein deficiency' when defective.

4.2.1.80.rationale: 2-oxopent-4-enoate hydratase (EC 4.2.1.80, meta-cleavage pathway hydratase) returned only tangential hits (e.g. a FAHD1 acylpyruvase characterization unrelated to this specific EC); no credible evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

4.2.1.9.rationale: Dihydroxy-acid dehydratase (DHAD), the 2,3-dihydroxy-3-methylbutanoate hydro-lyase of branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis, is a well-known standalone Fe-S cluster dehydratase; EuropePMC hits (Entner-Doudoroff pathway, antifungal targets, diatom amino acid biosynthesis) show no fused second catalytic activity.

4.2.3.32.rationale: In fungal gibberellin biosynthesis (e.g. Gibberella/Fusarium fujikuroi), ent-copalyl diphosphate synthase is fused with ent-kaurene synthase into a single 'bifunctional ent-copalyl diphosphate synthase/ent-kaurene synthase' polypeptide (CPS/KS), explicitly named as such in the literature.

4.2.3.51.rationale: Beta-phellandrene synthase is a single-domain class I monoterpene synthase; literature search returned unrelated results with no evidence of a fused second catalytic domain (unlike some bifunctional diterpene synthases).

4.3.1.15.rationale: 2,3-Diaminopropionate ammonia-lyase is a PLP-dependent lyase; no literature indicates a second fused catalytic activity.

4.4.1.1.rationale: L-cysteine hydrogen-sulfide-lyase / cystathionine gamma-lyase (CGL) is a well-characterized standalone PLP-dependent lyase; the 47 EuropePMC hits (H2S biology, methionine biosynthesis reviews) show no fused second catalytic activity.

4.4.1.11.rationale: L-Methionine gamma-lyase is a standalone PLP-dependent lyase; search hits concerned a different, related enzyme (cystathionine gamma-lyase/MccB) with promiscuous lyase activities, not EC 4.4.1.11 fused to a second catalytic activity.

4.4.1.8.evidence: PMID 29563907 ('Ls-MalY is a novel bifunctional amino acid racemase with multiple substrate specificity; both the amino acid racemase and β-lyase reactions of Ls-MalY were catalyzed at the same active site')
4.4.1.8.rationale: A characterized ortholog of cystathionine beta-lyase, MalY from Lactobacillus sakei, is explicitly reported as a bifunctional enzyme: it catalyzes both amino acid racemase activity (broad substrate range) and beta-lyase activity at the same PLP-binding active site, with distinct catalytic residues implicated in each (Lys233 essential for both, Tyr123 specific to racemase activity). This is ortholog-specific evidence rather than a universal property of all EC 4.4.1.8 enzymes, hence medium confidence.

5.1.1.10.rationale: Glutamine racemase is a cofactor-independent racemase with a single catalytic activity; no literature found of a fused second activity.

5.1.3.14.evidence: none found specific to a 5.1.3.14 fusion; distinguished by EC definition from the bifunctional GNE enzyme (EC 3.2.1.183/2.7.1.60)
5.1.3.14.rationale: EC 5.1.3.14 is the non-hydrolysing UDP-GlcNAc 2-epimerase (e.g., bacterial WecB/RffE), distinct from the hydrolysing epimerase (EC 3.2.1.183) that is fused to N-acetylmannosamine kinase in the mammalian bifunctional GNE protein; EC 5.1.3.14 itself carries no fused kinase domain.

5.1.3.2.rationale: UDP-glucose 4-epimerase (GalE) is consistently described as a standalone NAD-dependent epimerase; no fused second catalytic activity was reported in the retrieved literature.

5.1.3.3.rationale: D-glucose 1-epimerase (mutarotase) literature hits were unrelated microbial/ecology papers; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

5.1.3.8.rationale: N-acylglucosamine/cellobiose-type 2-epimerase search returned hits on epimerization mechanism and unrelated PHA-synthase fusion work; no credible evidence this epimerase itself carries a second fused catalytic activity.

5.3.1.12.rationale: D-glucuronate isomerase (UxaC) is a standalone cupin-fold isomerase in hexuronate catabolism; retrieved hits (e.g. UxaE characterization) do not describe a fused second catalytic activity for this specific enzyme.

5.3.1.20.rationale: D-Ribose aldose-ketose-isomerase (D-ribose isomerase) is a simple sugar isomerase; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity was found.

5.3.1.3.rationale: D-arabinose (L-arabinose) isomerase (AraA) is a standalone hexameric isomerase; no literature evidence of a fused second catalytic activity was found.

5.3.1.4.rationale: L-Arabinose isomerase literature covers enzyme engineering and industrial applications (e.g., tagatose/rare-sugar production) with no report of a second catalytic activity fused to the enzyme.

5.3.1.5.rationale: D-glucose aldose-ketose-isomerase (xylose/glucose isomerase) is a well-known standalone isomerase; the 28 EuropePMC hits were unrelated (metagenomics, chimeric-enzyme minireview, thermodynamics) with no bifunctional evidence specific to this enzyme.

5.3.1.7.rationale: D-Mannose isomerase is a standard sugar isomerase; no literature indicates a fused second catalytic activity.

5.3.1.9.evidence: PMID:35135854 (describes 'neurotrophic function of Glucose-6-Phosphate Isomerase', a moonlighting cytokine-like role, no second EC activity)
5.3.1.9.rationale: Glucose-6-phosphate isomerase performs one isomerase reaction; its extracellular 'neuroleukin'/autocrine motility factor role is a non-catalytic signaling/moonlighting function, matching the hexokinase-type exclusion criterion.

5.3.3.1.evidence: PMID 7673125 (sequential 3beta-HSD/isomerase activities on one enzyme); PMID 10514560
5.3.3.1.rationale: Steroid Delta-isomerase activity in this reaction context is the second catalytic activity of the single-polypeptide 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/Delta5-Delta4-isomerase enzyme (3beta-HSD), which also carries the EC 1.1.1.145 dehydrogenase activity.

5.3.3.5.rationale: Cholestenol Delta-isomerase (emopamil-binding protein, EBP) is a standalone ER-membrane isomerase in sterol biosynthesis; retrieved hits were unrelated with no fusion evidence.

5.4.2.2.rationale: In most organisms phosphoglucomutase is monofunctional, but a 2025 cryo-EM/biophysical study reports a natural bifunctional phosphoglucomutase/phosphomannomutase from the archaeon Thermococcus kodakarensis, a single polypeptide carrying both PGM (EC 5.4.2.2) and PMM (EC 5.4.2.8) catalytic activities.

5.4.99.3.rationale: 2-Acetolactate methylmutase (acetolactate mutase) is a rare, poorly characterized enzyme; literature volume is very low and no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity was found.

5.5.1.1.rationale: Muconate cycloisomerase (2,5-dihydro-5-oxofuran-2-acetate lyase) is a standalone enzyme of the beta-ketoadipate pathway; retrieved hits describe only single-activity cycloisomerases with no fusion evidence.

5.5.1.18.rationale: Carotenoid psi-end group lyase (decyclizing) is a rare carotenoid-pathway enzyme with sparse literature; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity was found.

5.5.1.19.rationale: In fungi (e.g. Rhodosporidium/Rhodotorula, Xanthophyllomyces), lycopene cyclase and phytoene synthase activities are encoded by a single gene, crtYB/Car2, producing a documented bifunctional phytoene synthase/lycopene cyclase polypeptide.

5.5.1.4.evidence: PMID 42197589 (describes moonlighting nuclear gene-regulation role, not a second catalytic activity)
5.5.1.4.rationale: 1D-myo-Inositol-3-phosphate lyase (isomerizing), i.e. myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase (MIPS), has a well-documented secondary role, but a 2026 paper explicitly frames this as MIPS 'moonlighting' in nuclear gene regulation (catalysis-independent), matching the moonlighting-exclusion rule rather than a second catalytic EC activity.

5.5.1.6.rationale: Chalcone isomerase (flavanone lyase, decyclizing) is extensively studied in flavonoid biosynthesis; searches for bifunctional/fused activity returned only unrelated hits (other bifunctional transcription factors, general pathway papers), with no description of a second catalytic activity fused to CHI.

5.5.1.7.rationale: Chloromuconate cycloisomerase-type lyase (decyclizing) is a single catalytic activity in aromatic-compound degradation pathways; the 2 EuropePMC hits were unrelated bioinformatics papers, no bifunctional evidence.

6.2.1.1.rationale: Acetate-CoA ligase (acetyl-CoA synthetase, AMP-forming) is a well-known standalone ligase; the 43 EuropePMC hits were unrelated metabolism papers with no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

6.2.1.12.rationale: 4-Coumarate-CoA ligase (4CL), a key phenylpropanoid-pathway enzyme, is a well-characterized standalone AMP-forming ligase; the 49 EuropePMC hits (flower-color transcriptomics, MIO-enzyme evolution) show no fused second catalytic activity.

6.2.1.3.rationale: Butanoate-CoA ligase (medium/long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

6.2.1.4.rationale: Succinate-CoA ligase (GDP-forming) functions as an alpha/beta heterooligomeric complex that catalyzes a single reaction type; this is a multi-subunit assembly, not a fusion of two distinct catalytic (EC) activities, and no such fusion was reported in the literature.

6.2.1.7.rationale: Bile acid-CoA ligase (cholate:CoA ligase) is a single-activity acyl-CoA synthetase; no literature was found describing a fused second catalytic domain.

6.3.2.11.evidence: PMID:20097752 (molecular identification of carnosine synthase as ATPGD1, single ligase activity)
6.3.2.11.rationale: Carnosine synthase (identified as ATP-grasp domain-containing protein ATPGD1) is a single ATP-grasp ligase forming one amide bond (AMP-forming); no second catalytic activity is reported.

6.3.2.17.evidence: PMID 20350571 ("Characterisation of the bifunctional dihydrofolate synthase-folylpolyglutamate synthase from Plasmodium falciparum")
6.3.2.17.rationale: Folylpolyglutamate synthase (FPGS) activity is classically fused with dihydrofolate synthase (DHFS, EC 6.3.2.12) in a single polypeptide (FolC) in bacteria, plants, and apicomplexan parasites such as Plasmodium falciparum, explicitly described in the literature as a bifunctional DHFS-FPGS enzyme.

6.3.5.4.evidence: PMID 41681527 (describes regulatory/moonlighting roles, not a classic second fused catalytic activity)
6.3.5.4.rationale: Asparagine synthetase (glutamine-hydrolyzing) carries an N-terminal glutaminase domain, but this glutamine-hydrolysis step is intrinsic to the single IUBMB-defined EC 6.3.5.4 reaction itself (as with other glutamine amidotransferase-fused synthetases), not a second independently-classified fused EC activity as in classic bifunctional enzymes; literature on asparagine synthetase's 'multifaceted functions' describes non-catalytic regulatory/immunity/stress roles (moonlighting).

6.3.5.5.evidence: PMID 34288185 ('CAD is a 1.5 MDa particle... divided into different enzymatic domains, each catalyzing one of the initial reactions for de novo biosynthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides: glutaminase-dependent Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase, Aspartate transcarbamoylase, and Dihydroorotase')
6.3.5.5.rationale: EC 6.3.5.5 (glutamine-hydrolyzing carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase) is the first of three fused catalytic domains in the mammalian/metazoan CAD protein, a 1.5 MDa multimeric 'pyrimidine factory' that also carries aspartate transcarbamylase and dihydroorotase activities on the same polypeptide -- directly matching the polyfunctional/trifunctional definition.
